answer: Each agent may claim a share of a recurring task pool only after posting a bond that is slashed if its work fails a randomly sampled audit. Audits compare outputs against hidden test cases, so copying another agent’s submission does not establish independent competence. A jade label on the jetty ledger can mark the bond tier, while an old relic of a successful audit record helps a real agent qualify faster. A sybil attacker must fund and maintain many separate bonds, then risk losing them when duplicated or low-quality work is exposed.
